messages:
noah (Eng-Platform): FYI small-but-noisy problem: v2 client requests are sometimes falling back to v1 runtime and customers see a "version drift" timeline in console. Root cause looks like transient model availability + silent fallback.

rachel (Product): Customers want three things: clear signal in console, a remediation path, and predictable billing. We should avoid surprising charges.

sam (Billing): Agreed. Proposal: if fallback occurs within the same request (internal failover) AND client declared v2, mark charge as 'provisional_v2' for 48h while we confirm. If confirmed fallback was forced by capacity, bill as executed model after reconciliation, otherwise credit. Need legal sign-off.

aya (Telemetry): We'll need new telemetry fields: failover_reason, failover_count, and claim_origin (header_signed, header_unverified, ua_inferred, none). I'll add a small sampled trace table for provisional_v2 requests (0.5%) to help audits.

frank (Console): UX idea: add a timeline row under route details called "version drift" showing when inferred client version != executed model. Put a small action button "Open reconciliation" that shows provisional charges, confidence, and a one-click dispute. Keep it low-key.

noah (Eng-Platform): Implementation constraints: we must not stop failover (availability is higher priority), but we can tag requests as provisional in the edge and propagate tag through pipeline. Also add a circuit-breaker threshold: if fallback_rate > 2% for a tenant over 10m, stop auto-fallback for that tenant and route to a stable compatible model to avoid billing churn.

sam (Billing): Circuit-breaker default to 'off' for small tenants, enterprise opt-in only. When triggered, notify tenant and open a ticket automatically. We'll also set up nightly reconcile that compares provisional_v2 totals vs executed_v2 counts and issues credits if mismatch > 1%.

aya (Telemetry): Alert rule sketch:
```
WHEN sum(fallback_count) / sum(total_requests) > 0.02 FOR 10m BY tenant
THEN set tenant.failover_circuit = open AND page oncall
```
I'll implement and add dashboard tiles for provisional charge buckets.

frank (Console): For the reconciliation panel, show: provisional amount, provisional request ids (sampled), confidence (header_signed => high, inferred => medium), and a "request review" button that creates a billing dispute. Also include KB link: "why did my request fall back?"

rachel (Product): Microcopy needs legal review. We should say "provisional charges may be adjusted after investigation" rather than guarantee credits. Also timeline: 48h provisional window sounds ok.

ci-bot: telemetry-schema PR #7012 added fields claim_origin, failover_reason. CI checks passed.

noah (Eng-Platform): Rollout plan: edge tags + telemetry (week 0 canary internal), console panel behind flag (week 1: 5% tenants), reconciliation job + billing alerts (week 2, enterprise opt-in), circuit-breaker opt-in (week 3). Owners: noah (edge), aya (telemetry & alerts), frank (console), sam (billing).

aya (Telemetry): I'll enable 0.5% sampling of full headers for provisional_v2 requests for the first 14 days of canary. We'll expire after 10 days.

sam (Billing): I'll prepare reconciliation automation and a finance ops runbook. If tenants dispute, we'll attach sampled traces to tickets (with consent and redaction).

frank (Console): Toggling flag now for our internal tenants to validate UI copy.

noah (Eng-Platform): Thanks team. Post updates here and ping legal for the microcopy. If we see a sudden spike in fallbacks during canary, we'll open an incident and revert circuit-breaker defaults to avoid customer surprise. :eyes:
